body:
WHAT
Prompt Lab is a local HTTP server on 127.0.0.1:4319 that shows every prompt the engine sends. GET /api/catalog returns the live prompt registry (default text, current text, token estimates, override directory, orphan files, an assembled system-prompt preview, review notes and per-prompt promotability). GET /api/events is a Server-Sent Events stream that pushes a 'changed' message when an override file changes on disk.

WHY
Without a catalog built from the real registry the console would show a reconstruction that drifts from what the engine actually sends; without the event stream a browser tab would not learn about edits made by another editor or by the engine.

WHERE
tools/prompt-lab/server.mjs — catalog() (uses protocol.promptCatalog(), estimateTokens(), promptsDir(), orphanedPromptFiles(), systemPreview() via core.buildSystemPrompt), markAddressed(), promotable(), the createServer handler branches for '/api/catalog' and '/api/events', broadcast(), startWatching() (fs.watch on promptsDir()), the module-load imports of @magentra/core, @magentra/tools and tools.createDefaultRegistry() that populate the registry; constants PORT/HOST via arg(); engine/protocol/src/prompts.ts — promptCatalog(), promptsDir().

TEST CHECKLIST
1. Start the server with --port 0-like free port and --dir pointing at an empty temp directory; GET /api/catalog returns 200 JSON whose prompts array has the same length and ids as promptCatalog() from @magentra/protocol after createDefaultRegistry(), and whose dir equals the temp directory.
2. Each catalog entry carries numeric defaultTokens and currentTokens, and the response has preview.system (non-empty string), preview.systemTokens and preview.toolTokens equal to the sum of currentTokens over entries with channel 'tool'.
3. Write <id>.txt into the override directory for one known prompt id from outside the server; the next GET /api/catalog shows that entry with overridden true and currentText equal to the file content, and a client connected to /api/events receives a data frame {type:'changed', id:<id>} within a few seconds.
4. GET /api/events answers 200 with content-type text/event-stream and an initial ': connected' comment line, and closing the client removes it from the clients set (a subsequent broadcast does not throw).
5. An unknown path returns 404 'not found', and the server binds only to 127.0.0.1 (connecting via another interface address fails).
